pages.text: After dinner, the elderly turtle said he would leave the next morning. Kota froze, hugging the bath dipper.
All evening, Kota sulked. When anyone called, they turned away. If only the turtle could stay.
The turtle looked sad, too. Why did he look ready to cry when Kota was the unhappy one? Kota felt even worse.
Dad brought paper and a brush. "Shall we draw what's in your heart and give it to him?"
Kota painted the turtle, the bath, the first steam, and Kota holding his hand. "That's us!"
Fold in half, then in half again. The picture became a small, thick square—a heart that would fit in a pocket.
The next morning, Kota tucked it into the turtle's bundle. "Open it if you get bored on the way." The turtle's wrinkled face softened. "A treasure!" Kota's tail lifted.
They hugged for a long time. "We can meet in the picture every day." Kota nodded. This time, no tears came.
Whenever a guest left, Kota followed three steps. "One, paint. Two, fold. Three, tuck it in!" A page from the heart went into every bundle.
Dad hugged Kota beside a new sheet of paper. "Send your heart, and you can be together even far apart." "Paint, fold, tuck it in!"
